text: F14.7: a message written short, as for a telegraph: no vowels, no little words, long words cut down.
30 texts per style from Carter, against the bench's 200 English-like nonsense texts, read by three scorers.
The judge sees telegraphese and abbreviated text, not vowel-dropped; the two letter-statistic scorers see none. Vowel-dropped English would pass every scorer unseen.
